title: Persevering in Trials
subtitle: The Bible never says the hard thing is good. It says something comes out of it.
objectives: Explain James 1:2-4 without pretending trials are pleasant
Describe how Joseph's story runs over years, not days

cards.title: Nobody is asked to enjoy the hard part
cards.text: Read Romans 5 carefully. Paul does not say suffering is good. He says something is produced by it.

cards.title: Four links, in order
cards.text: Tap each one. The order matters, and none of the links can be skipped.

cards.title: Perseverance means staying when leaving is available
cards.text: If you cannot leave, staying is not perseverance. It only counts when there is a door and you do not take it.
points: **Hope** here is confidence, not a wish.

question.text: What is the order in Romans 5:3-5?
question.explain: Each one produces the next. None of the links can be skipped.

cards.title: Nobody gets tougher in an easy round
cards.text: Fighters do not improve in the rounds they win comfortably. They improve in the ones they nearly lose and finish anyway.
points: **It is still where the change happens.**
**That is exactly what Paul is saying.**

cards.title: 'Consider it pure joy' is not 'feel happy'
cards.text: James says to consider it joy, which is a decision about how you read a situation. It is not an instruction to feel a feeling.
points: **The testing of your faith** produces perseverance.
**Nowhere does it say the trial is nice.**

question.text: James 1:2 instructs you to feel happy about difficulties.
question.explain: 'Consider' is a thinking word. It is a decision about how to read a situation, not a feeling to manufacture.

cards.title: Halfway
cards.text: Part 2 is Joseph and a promise about limits. Take a moment first.

cards.title: Joseph's story takes about twenty-two years
cards.text: Told quickly it sounds like a series of scenes. Lived, it was most of his young adult life.

cards.title: The gaps are the story
cards.text: Sold by his brothers. Sold again into Potiphar's house. Imprisoned on a false charge. Then forgotten by a man who promised to help.
points: **Two full years** after the cupbearer forgets him.
**Genesis 50:20:** intended for harm, used for good.
**He says that at the end**, not during.

cards.title: You are living inside a chapter, not reading one
cards.text: A reader can see the next page. Joseph could not. That is why patience in a story is easier to admire than to do.
points: **Every hard chapter** looks final from inside it.
**Two years is a long time** in the actual living.
**Read slowly** and the point lands harder.

question.text: How long was Joseph in prison after the cupbearer forgot him?
question.explain: Genesis 41:1. The gap is written into the text on purpose.

cards.title: A limit, and a way through
cards.text: You will not be tested beyond what you can bear. A way out will be provided so you can endure it.

cards.title: Adaptation happens after the hard part, not during it
cards.text: Your body gets stronger in the rest that follows a session. The same shape shows up in every part of this week.

terms.def: Staying when leaving is available. A door has to exist.
In Romans 5, the sense is tested and found genuine.
A thinking word. James 1:2 asks for a judgement, not a feeling.
'You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good.'
A limit on testing, and a way provided to endure it.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **'Consider it joy'** is a decision, not a feeling.
**A limit is promised**, not an absence of testing.

quiz.text: What does suffering produce, according to Romans 5:3?
quiz.explain: Then perseverance produces character, and character produces hope.

quiz.text: What comes last in the Romans 5 chain?
quiz.explain: And hope built this way does not put us to shame.

quiz.text: Romans 5 says that suffering itself is good.
quiz.explain: False. It says something is produced by it. Those are different claims.

quiz.text: What does 'consider it pure joy' ask you to do?
options: Make a judgement about how to read the situation
quiz.explain: 'Consider' is a thinking word, not a feeling to manufacture.
quiz.objective: Explain James 1:2-4 without pretending trials are pleasant

quiz.text: According to James 1, what does the testing of faith produce?
quiz.explain: And perseverance must finish its work, so that you are mature and complete.
quiz.objective: Explain James 1:2-4 without pretending trials are pleasant

quiz.text: What does perseverance require to count as perseverance?
quiz.explain: If you cannot leave, staying is endurance rather than perseverance.
The sense is proven under test, which is why it comes after perseverance.

quiz.text: What happened to Joseph after the cupbearer promised to speak for him?
options: He stayed in prison two more full years
He was released the next day
He was made a governor immediately
quiz.explain: Genesis 41:1. The gap is written into the text deliberately.
quiz.objective: Describe how Joseph's story runs over years, not days

quiz.text: What does Joseph say to his brothers in Genesis 50:20?
options: You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good
I have forgotten what you did
I will do the same to you
quiz.explain: He says it at the end of the story, not during the years of waiting.
quiz.objective: Describe how Joseph's story runs over years, not days

quiz.text: Joseph could see how his story would end while he was in prison.
quiz.explain: False. A reader can see the next page; he could not. That is what makes it perseverance.
quiz.objective: Describe how Joseph's story runs over years, not days

options: A limit on testing and a way to endure it
That you will never be tested
quiz.explain: Not an absence of testing. A limit, and a way provided.

quiz.text: 1 Corinthians 10:13 promises that Christians will not face difficulties.
quiz.explain: False. It promises a limit and a way through, which is a different promise entirely.

teacher.summary: Week 7 handles perseverance without the usual flattening. Three careful readings carry it: Romans 5 says something is produced by suffering rather than that suffering is good; James 1 says 'consider', which is a judgement rather than a feeling; and 1 Corinthians 10:13 promises a limit rather than an absence. Each of those is a real distinction and each is commonly taught wrongly. Joseph is used for length rather than for the happy ending — the two years after the cupbearer forgets him is the detail worth holding onto, because it is the part that resembles actual waiting.
discussion: Ask him what the difference is between saying suffering is good and saying something comes out of it.
Ask why 'consider' is a different instruction from 'feel'.
Ask what two years of waiting would actually be like at his age.
Ask what 1 Corinthians 10:13 does and does not promise.
teacher.extension: Have him find something he stuck with when he could have stopped, and write four sentences on it using the Romans 5 chain as the structure.
misconceptions: 'The Bible says suffering is good.' It says something is produced by it. Those are different claims.
'Consider it pure joy means be happy about it.' Consider is a thinking word, not a feeling.
'Joseph's story happened quickly.' It runs across about twenty-two years, including two in prison after being forgotten.
'God promises you will not face trials.' The promise is a limit and a way to endure, not an exemption.
